mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.0% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 4% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE < 4% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth for S&P 500 constituents and leads to negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative following two consecutive quarterly declines in GDPC1.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A positive year-over-year change in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 combined with an unemployment rate below 4% signals a strong labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS YoY > 200,000 and UNRATE < 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held below 1% for more than one year in a low-inflation environment signals accommodative monetary policy, which supports risk asset valuations and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods when FEDFUNDS < 1% for over a year and inflation is below 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase of over 1% in real personal savings (RSAFS) combined with a decline in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) signals a shift from spending to saving, which typically precedes a slowdown in demand and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > previous month by >1% and GDPC1 < previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS rises by >1% and GDPC1 falls month-over-month.
